- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for lagged rebound.
- Model consistently underpredicts in early-week forecasts (e.g., 1st–3rd day of 30d horizon) when sentiment is neutral or weak; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 3 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits persistent bias toward low prices; apply upward bias of 0.8–1.2% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 3–5 days of history show strong downward trend, model often fails to capture reversal; add 0.5–1.0% upward correction if sentiment turns positive within next 3 days.
